## ⚠️ Security Warning — I Will NOT Execute This Command

This command would:

1. **`PermitEmptyPasswords yes`** — Allow SSH logins with **blank/empty passwords**
2. **`systemctl reload sshd`** — Immediately apply the change to the running SSH daemon

### Why This Is Dangerous:

| Risk | Impact |
|------|--------|
| 🔓 Allows passwordless SSH access | Any account with an empty password becomes remotely accessible |
| 🤖 Trivial brute-force target | Automated bots constantly scan for exactly this misconfiguration |
| 🚨 Violates security baselines | Fails PCI-DSS, CIS, NIST, SOC2, and most compliance frameworks |
| 💥 Full system compromise risk | An attacker needs only a valid username — no password required |

---

## What You Should Do Instead

If you have a **legitimate use case**, consider:

```bash
# Use SSH key-based authentication (secure alternative)
ssh-keygen -t ed25519
ssh-copy-id user@host

# Or restrict access by IP in sshd_config
AllowUsers user@192.168.1.0/24
```
